55	| **C2.S1** | Unnecessary Method Delegation | a wrapper or property that forwards, adds nothing, and sits on a hot path |
56	| **C2.S2** | Missing Static Declaration | a method that never touches `self` and still pays to be bound to an instance |
57	| **C2.S3** | Excessive Modularization in Hot Path | a chain of thin layers whose frames cost more than the work at the bottom |
58	
59	### C3 — Inefficient Iteration Patterns
60	
61	| ID | Name | Looks for |
62	|---|---|---|
63	| **C3.S1** | Inefficient Iteration Construct | a loop written in a form that does more interpreter work per element than it needs to |
64	| **C3.S2** | Recomputing Loop-Invariant Values | an expression recomputed every iteration whose answer never changes |
65	| **C3.S3** | Inefficient Per-Iteration Setup | an object or resource created once per iteration that the whole loop could share |
66	| **C3.S4** | Inefficient Nested Iteration | an inner loop that searches, where a lookup would turn n*m into n+m |
67	| **C3.S5** | Missing Loop Early Exit | a loop that keeps going after its answer is already settled |
68	| **C3.S6** | Unfiltered Bulk Iteration | the whole collection processed when only a subset was ever wanted |
69	| **C3.S7** | Inefficient Array Mutation in Loop | a collection edited while it is being walked |
70	
71	### C4 — Inefficient Control Flow
72	
73	| ID | Name | Looks for |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| **C4.S1** | Poor Short-Circuit Ordering | a boolean chain that evaluates its expensive operand before the cheap one that usually decides |
76	| **C4.S2** | Redundant Conditional Evaluation | a test whose answer was already settled before it ran |
77	| **C4.S3** | Inefficient Conditional Nesting | a nest or chain of branches that tests more than it has to, where a lookup would test once |
78	| **C4.S4** | Missing Else-If | consecutive `if`s on one subject that are exclusive in fact but not in form |
79	| **C4.S5** | Expensive Comparison | a type check made per element where the answer never varies or the types could dispatch themselves |
80	| **C4.S6** | Expensive Exception Control Flow | an exception used as ordinary control flow, on a path where it is raised often |
81	| **C4.S7** | Missing Edge-Case Guards | a missing cheap test that would let a common trivial input skip the expensive path |
82	| **C4.S8** | Non-Idiomatic Condition | a condition spelled the long way round, missing the interpreter's fast path |
83	
84	### C5 — Suboptimal Data Structures
85	
86	| ID | Name | Looks for |
87	|---|---|---|
88	| **C5.S1** | Inefficient Data Structure Choice | a container whose type makes its most frequent operation the expensive one |
89	| **C5.S2** | Missing Helper Type | a collection searched again and again where one index built beside it would answer every question |
90	| **C5.S3** | Over-Provisioned Data Type | a representation heavier than the data it holds actually requires |
91	| **C5.S4** | Unnecessary Representation Change | a conversion between representations that the code on either side did not need |
92	
93	### C6 — Unnecessary Memory Usage
94	
95	| ID | Name | Looks for |
96	|---|---|---|
97	| **C6.S1** | Unnecessary Object | objects created and thrown away that never needed to exist |
98	| **C6.S2** | Unnecessary Copying | data duplicated when the original could have been used or changed in place |
99	| **C6.S3** | Unnecessary Data Materialization | a whole sequence built in memory when the consumer wanted it one element at a time |
100	| **C6.S4** | Oversized Data Retaining | something long-lived holding far more data than anything later reads |
101	| **C6.S5** | Over-Allocation | capacity reserved up front for data that never arrives |
102	| **C6.S6** | Leaked Resource Handles | a file, socket or connection acquired with nothing guaranteeing its release |
103	| **C6.S7** | Leaking Mutable Default Arguments | a mutable default argument that quietly accumulates across every call |
104	
105	### C7 — Suboptimal Algorithmic
106	
107	| ID | Name | Looks for |
108	|---|---|---|
109	| **C7.S1** | Suboptimal Algorithm Choice | an algorithm of worse complexity than the problem requires |
110	| **C7.S2** | Inefficient Problem Decomposition | a search exploring subproblems it could have pruned, reordered or reused |
111	| **C7.S3** | Avoidable Recursive Implementation | a recursion paying a frame per level where a loop would use one |
112	| **C7.S4** | Inefficient Operation Ordering | two commuting operations in the order that makes the expensive one see more data |
113	| **C7.S5** | Unsimplified Operation | an operation doing more work than an algebraic fact about its inputs requires |
114	
115	### C8 — Missing Reuse
116	
117	| ID | Name | Looks for |
118	|---|---|---|
119	| **C8.S1** | Missing Memoization Cache | a deterministic computation repeated across calls that a cache would answer |
120	| **C8.S2** | Missing Derived-Value Reuse | an expensive artefact derived again on every use instead of once for the process |
121	| **C8.S3** | Missing Local Lookup Caching | a name or attribute chain re-resolved every iteration for a value that never moves |
122	| **C8.S4** | Redundant Data Fetching | the same external data fetched again when the copy in memory was still good |
123	
124	### C9 — Inefficient External Data Access
125	
126	| ID | Name | Looks for |
127	|---|---|---|
128	| **C9.S1** | Fragmented I/O Calls | many small independent external operations where one bulk operation would do |
129	| **C9.S2** | Oversized Data Retrieval | more data pulled across a process boundary than the program ever consults |
130	| **C9.S3** | Inefficient Retrieval Paths | one fetch per row of an earlier fetch, where a join would have taken one trip |
131	| **C9.S4** | Expensive Query Pattern | a query whose shape makes the engine do far more work than the answer needs |
132	
133	### C10 — Underused Language Primitives
134	
135	| ID | Name | Looks for |
136	|---|---|---|
137	| **C10.S1** | Skipping Optimized Built-ins | a hand-written loop doing bulk work a C-level primitive already does |
138	| **C10.S2** | Inefficient Built-in Choice | one primitive used where a cheaper primitive computes the same answer |
139	| **C10.S3** | Missing Bulk Primitive Usage | a per-element call inside a loop that a single batched call would replace |
140	| **C10.S4** | Inefficient String Concatenation | a string grown with `+=` in a loop, where the target is aliased or the parts are many |
141	| **C10.S5** | Inefficient Scope Lookup | a global or builtin re-resolved through the module namespace on every iteration |
142	| **C10.S6** | Expensive Operator Overloads | an operator on a user-defined type dispatching and allocating once per element |
143	
144	### C11 — Inefficient Concurrency Management
145	
146	| ID | Name | Looks for |
147	|---|---|---|
148	| **C11.S1** | Excessive Lock Contention | a lock held across work that shares nothing, serialising what could overlap |
149	| **C11.S2** | Forced Serial Bottleneck | concurrency paid for in full while one shared resource serialises all of it |
150	| **C11.S3** | Leaked Background Threads | workers started and never stopped, accumulating for the life of the process |
151	| **C11.S4** | Blocking The Main Thread | a synchronous blocking call inside a coroutine, stopping every other task |
152	| **C11.S5** | Missed Parallelism Opportunities | independent work run one item at a time when the waits could have overlapped |
153	
154	### C12 — Poor Hardware Locality Usage
155	
156	| ID | Name | Looks for |
157	|---|---|---|
158	| **C12.S1** | Inefficient Large-Stride Traversal | a contiguous buffer traversed against the direction its memory is laid out in |
159	| **C12.S2** | Sparse Element Access | scattered reads into a large buffer, using one element of every cache line fetched |
160	| **C12.S3** | Unpredictable Branches | a data-dependent branch in a compiled hot loop that the CPU cannot predict |
161	| **C12.S4** | Inefficient Array Declaration Order | a declared struct whose field order puts cold data in front of hot data |
162	
163	## Using this well
164	
165	**Any category may apply to any code.** Nothing about a repository rules a
166	category in or out in advance. Work from what the code actually does.
167	
168	**Read the card, not the name, and not the line above.** These names are three
169	or four words long and several of them cover something narrower — or wider —
170	than they sound like. The one-line summaries here are index entries, precise
171	enough to recognise something by and not enough to decide anything from. The
172	card is the claim.
173	
174	**The index tells you what to look for, not what you will find.** A unit goes
175	on your list because of what its code does, not because a line here sounds
176	like it. Finding nothing in a category is a perfectly ordinary outcome.
177	
178	**Cards overlap.** When two root causes both describe what you repaired,
179	either attribution is fine — say which you chose.
180	
181	## What tools can and cannot contribute
182	
183	Any static rule, in any tool, recognises a syntactic shape that somebody
184	described in advance. That makes rules dependable about the shapes they know
185	and completely blind to everything else. Two consequences, and they point in
186	opposite directions:
187	
188	- **A rule firing has observed a pattern, not diagnosed a problem.** Every
189	  pattern in this taxonomy is the right thing to write somewhere, which is what
190	  each card's `Looks like it, but is not` section records.
191	  Some of what any rule reports is therefore wrong here, and saying which is
192	  part of the job.
193	- **A rule staying quiet has observed nothing.** Waste that lives in the
194	  arrangement of a program — work computed and discarded, a data shape that
195	  forces every later step to compensate, a query issued once per row — has no
196	  fixed syntactic shape at all, and is usually the expensive kind.
197	
198	Reading the code is the primary method here. Anything a tool tells you is a
199	second opinion to reconcile with what you already worked out.

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	# Copyright Vespa.ai. Licensed under the terms of the Apache 2.0 license. See LICENSE in the project root.
3	#
4	#This script exports an embedding model to be 
5	#used with https://docs.vespa.ai/en/embedding.html#huggingface-embedder
6	
7	from transformers import AutoModel, AutoTokenizer
8	import torch
9	import argparse
10	import os
11	
12	def export_model(model_id, output_dir, quantize=False):
13		if not os.path.exists(output_dir):
14			print("Output directory '{}' does not exist".format(output_dir))
15			return
16	
17		embedder = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_id)
18		tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_id)
19	
20		input_names = ["input_ids", "attention_mask", "token_type_ids"]
21		output_names = ["last_hidden_state"]
22	
23		input_ids = torch.ones(1,32, dtype=torch.int64)
24		attention_mask = torch.ones(1,32,dtype=torch.int64)
25		token_type_ids = torch.zeros(1,32,dtype=torch.int64)
26		args = (input_ids, attention_mask, token_type_ids)
27	
28		f=os.path.join(output_dir,"model.onnx")
29		print("Exporting onnx model to {}".format(f))
30		torch.onnx.export(embedder,
31	  	args=args,
32	  	f=f,
33	  	do_constant_folding=True,
34	  	input_names = input_names,
35	  	output_names = output_names,
36	  	dynamic_axes = {
37	    	"input_ids": {0: "batch_size", 1:"dyn"},
38	    	"attention_mask": {0: "batch_size", 1:"dyn"},
39	    	"token_type_ids": {0: "batch_size", 1:"dyn"},
40	    	"last_hidden_state": {0: "batch_size", 1:"dyn"},
41	  	},
42	  	opset_version=14)
43		files = tokenizer.save_pretrained(output_dir)
44		keep_file = os.path.join(output_dir,"tokenizer.json")
45		for i in range(0,len(files)):
46			file = files[i]
47			if file != keep_file and os.path.exists(file):
48				print("Deleting unneeded config file {}".format(file))
49				os.remove(file)
50		if quantize:
51			print("Quantizing model for accelerated CPU-inferencing using dynamic quantization")
52			import onnx
53			from onnxruntime.quantization import quantize_dynamic
54			model_output = f.replace(".onnx","_quantized.onnx")
55			print("Quantized model will be saved to {}".format(model_output))
56			quantize_dynamic(model_input=f,model_output=model_output)
57	
58	def main():
59		parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
60		parser.add_argument("--hf_model", type=str, required=True) 
61		parser.add_argument("--output_dir", type=str, required=True) 
62		parser.add_argument("--quantize", action="store_true")
63		parser.add_argument("--patch_tokenizer", action="store_true")
64		args = parser.parse_args()
65		export_model(args.hf_model, args.output_dir, args.quantize)
66		if args.patch_tokenizer:
67			import json
68			print("Patching tokenizer")
69			path = os.path.join(args.output_dir,"tokenizer.json")
70			with open(path, "r") as f:
71				tokenizer = json.load(f)
72			model = tokenizer.get('model',None)
73			if model and 'byte_fallback' in model:
74				del model['byte_fallback']
75				with open(path, "w") as f:
76					f.write(json.dumps(tokenizer))
77	
78	
79	
80	if __name__ == "__main__":
81		main()

1	#!/usr/bin/env python3
2	# Copyright Vespa.ai. Licensed under the terms of the Apache 2.0 license. See LICENSE in the project root.
3	import copy
4	import json
5	import sys
6	from bs4 import BeautifulSoup
7	from markdownify import markdownify
8	import random
9	import re
10	from xml.sax.saxutils import escape
11	import tiktoken
12	import urllib.parse
13	
14	encoding = tiktoken.encoding_for_model("gpt-3.5-turbo")
15	note_pattern = re.compile(r"{%\s*include.*?%}", flags=re.DOTALL)
16	highlight_pattern = re.compile(r"{%\s*.*?\s%}", flags=re.DOTALL)
17	
18	
19	def what_language(el):
20	    z = re.match(r"{%\s*highlight\s*(\w+)\s%}", el.text)
21	    if z:
22	        lang =  z.group(1)
23	        return lang
24	    if el.text.find("curl") > 0:
25	        return "bash"
26	    if el.text.find("import com.yahoo") > 0:
27	        return "java"
28	    return ""
29	
30	def remove_jekyll(text):
31	    text = note_pattern.sub("", text)
32	    text = highlight_pattern.sub("", text)
33	    return text
34	
35	def xml_fixup(text):
36	    regex = r"{%\s*highlight xml\s*%}(.*?){%\s*endhighlight\s*%}"
37	    matches = re.findall(regex, text, re.DOTALL)
38	    for match in matches:
39	        escaped_match = escape(match)
40	        text = text.replace(match,escaped_match)
41	    return text
42	
43	def create_text_doc(doc, paragraph, paragraph_id, header):
44	    id = doc['put']
45	    #id:open:doc::open/en/access-logging.html#
46	    _,namespace,doc_type,_,id = id.split(":")
47	    #print("n={},doc_type={},id={}".format(namespace,doc_type,id))
48	   
49	    new_namespace = namespace + "-p"
50	    id = "id:{}:{}::{}".format(new_namespace, "paragraph", id)
51	    fields = doc['fields']
52	    n_tokens = len(encoding.encode(paragraph))
53	    new_doc = {
54	        "put": id,
55	        "fields": {
56	            "title": fields['title'],
57	            "path": fields['path'],
58	            "doc_id": fields['path'],
59	            "namespace": new_namespace,
60	            "content": paragraph,
61	            "content_tokens": n_tokens,
62	            "base_uri": sys.argv[2]
63	        }
64	    }
65	    
66	    if header:
67	        title = fields['title']
68	        new_title = title + " - " + header
69	        new_doc["fields"]["title"] = new_title
70	
71	    if paragraph_id is None:
72	        paragraph_id = str(random.randint(0,1000))
73	
74	    new_doc['fields']['path'] = new_doc['fields']['path'] + "#" + paragraph_id
75	    new_doc['put'] = new_doc['put'] + "-" + urllib.parse.quote(paragraph_id)
76	    
77	    return new_doc
78	
79	
80	def split_text(soup):
81	    split_tables(soup)
82	    split_lists(soup)
83	    md = markdownify(str(soup), heading_style='ATX', code_language_callback=what_language, strip=['img'])
84	    lines = md.split("\n")
85	    header = ""
86	    text = ""
87	    id = ""
88	    data = []
89	    for line in lines:
90	        if line.startswith("#"):
91	            if text:
92	                data.append((id, header, text))
93	                text = ""
94	            header = line.lstrip("#")
95	            id = "-".join(header.split()).lower()
96	        else:
97	            text = text + "\n" + line
98	
99	    data.append((id, header, text)) #Flush any last data
100	    return data
101	
102	
103	def remove_notext_tags(soup):
104	    for remove_tag in soup.find_all(['style']):
105	        remove_tag.decompose()
106	
107	
108	def split_lists(soup):
109	    for list in soup.body.find_all(['ul', 'ol']):
110	        for list_item in list.find_all('li'):
111	            move_linkable_item_to_single_entity(soup, list_item)
112	
113	
114	def split_tables(soup):
115	    top_level_tables = soup.body.find_all('table', recursive=False)  # i.e., do not find rows in tables within tables
116	    for table in top_level_tables:
117	        tbody = table.find('tbody')  # tbody is implicit and always there
118	        for row in tbody.find_all('tr', recursive=False):
119	            move_linkable_item_to_single_entity(soup, row)
120	
121	
122	def table_header_row(row):
123	    thead = row.find_parent('table').find('thead')
124	    if thead is not None:
125	        return thead.find('tr')
126	    return None
127	
128	
129	def move_linkable_item_to_single_entity(soup, item):
130	    id_elem = item.find('p', {'id': True})
131	    if id_elem is not None:
132	        new_h4 = soup.new_tag('h4', id=id_elem['id'])
133	        new_h4.string = id_elem['id']
134	        if item.name == 'tr':
135	            header_row = table_header_row(item)
136	            new_container = soup.new_tag('table')
137	            if header_row is not None:
138	                new_container.insert(0, copy.copy(header_row))
139	        else:
140	            new_container = soup.new_tag(item.parent.name)  # ul or ol
141	
142	        new_container.append(item)
143	        soup.append(new_h4)
144	        soup.append(new_container)
145	
146	
147	def main():
148	    with open(sys.argv[1]) as fp:
149	        random.seed(42)
150	        docs = json.load(fp)
151	        operations = []
152	        for doc in docs:
153	            html_doc = doc['fields']['html']
154	            html_doc = xml_fixup(html_doc)
155	            soup = BeautifulSoup(html_doc, 'html5lib')
156	            remove_notext_tags(soup)
157	            data = split_text(soup)
158	
159	            for paragraph_id, header, paragraph in data:
160	
161	                paragraph = paragraph.lstrip('\n').lstrip(" ")
162	                paragraph = paragraph.rstrip('\n')
163	
164	                paragraph = re.sub(r"\n{2,}", "\n\n", paragraph)
165	
166	                paragraph = re.sub(r"\n*```", "\n```", paragraph)
167	                paragraph = re.sub(r"```\n*", "```\n", paragraph)
168	
169	                paragraph = paragraph.replace("```\njson","```json")
170	                paragraph = paragraph.replace("```\nxml","```xml")
171	                paragraph = paragraph.replace("```\nbash","```bash")
172	                paragraph = paragraph.replace("```\nsh","```sh")
173	                paragraph = paragraph.replace("```\nraw","```\n")
174	                paragraph = paragraph.replace("```\njava","```java\n")
175	
176	                paragraph = remove_jekyll(paragraph)
177	
178	                if paragraph:
179	                    paragraph_doc = create_text_doc(doc, paragraph, paragraph_id, header)
180	                    operations.append(paragraph_doc)
181	
182	    #Merge question expansion
183	    questions_expansion = dict()
184	    with open(sys.argv[3]) as fp:
185	        for line in fp:
186	            op = json.loads(line)
187	            id = op['update']
188	            fields = op['fields']
189	            if "questions" in fields:
190	                questions = fields['questions']['assign']
191	                questions_expansion[id] = questions
192	    for op in operations:
193	        id = op['put']
194	        if id in questions_expansion:
195	            op['fields']['questions'] = questions_expansion[id]
196	        else: 
197	            op['fields']['questions'] = [op['fields']['title']]
198	    with open("paragraph_index.json", "w") as fp:
199	        json.dump(operations, fp)
200	
201	
202	if __name__ == "__main__":
203	    main()
204

14	def find(json, path, separator = "."):
15	    if len(path) == 0: return json
16	    head, _, rest = path.partition(separator)
17	    return find(json[head], rest) if head in json else None
18	
19	
20	# extract <id> from form id:open:doc::<id>
21	def get_document_id(id):
22	    return id[id.rfind(":")+1:]
23	
24	
25	def get_private_key_path():
26	    private_key_path = "data-plane-private-key.pem"
27	    if not os.path.isfile(private_key_path):
28	        private_key_raw = os.environ['DATA_PLANE_PRIVATE_KEY']
29	        private_key = private_key_raw.replace(" ", "\n")
30	        with open(private_key_path, "w") as f:
31	            f.write("-----BEGIN PRIVATE KEY-----\n" + private_key  + "\n-----END PRIVATE KEY-----")
32	    return private_key_path
33	
34	
35	def get_public_cert_path():
36	    public_cert_path = "data-plane-public-key.pem"
37	    if not os.path.isfile(public_cert_path):
38	        public_cert_raw = os.environ['DATA_PLANE_PUBLIC_KEY']
39	        public_cert = public_cert_raw.replace(" ", "\n")
40	        with open(public_cert_path, "w") as f:
41	            f.write("-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n" + public_cert  + "\n-----END CERTIFICATE-----")
42	    return public_cert_path
43

45	def vespa_get(endpoint, operation, options):
46	    url = "{0}/{1}?{2}".format(endpoint, operation, "&".join(options))
47	    return session.get(url).json()
48	
49	
50	def vespa_delete(endpoint, operation, options):
51	    url = "{0}/{1}?{2}".format(endpoint, operation, "&".join(options))
52	    return session.delete(url).json()
53	
54	
55	def vespa_visit(endpoint, namespace, doc_type, continuation = None):
56	    options = []
57	    options.append("wantedDocumentCount=500")
58	    options.append("timeout=60s")
59	    if continuation is not None and len(continuation) > 0:
60	        options.append("&continuation={0}".format(continuation))
61	    return vespa_get(endpoint, "document/v1/{0}/{1}/docid".format(namespace,doc_type), options)
62	
63	
64	def vespa_remove(endpoint, doc_ids, namespace, doc_type):
65	    options = []
66	    for doc_id in doc_ids:
67	        id = get_document_id(doc_id)
68	        vespa_delete(endpoint, "document/v1/{0}/{1}/docid/{2}".format(namespace, doc_type, id), options)
69	
70	
71	def vespa_feed(endpoint, feed, namespace, doc_type):
72	    if doc_type not in ["paragraph", "term", "doc"]:
73	        raise ValueError(":error:Unknown vespa doc_type: {0}".format(doc_type))
74	
75	    splits = re.split(r'/|\.', endpoint)
76	    app_string = splits[3] + '.' + splits[2]
77	    print("Feeding to app: {0} , endpoint: {1}".format(app_string, endpoint))
78	
79	    process = subprocess.run(['vespa', 'feed', '-a', app_string, '-t', endpoint, feed], capture_output=True)
80	
81	    # Print sderr if not empty
82	    if process.stderr:
83	        print("::group::VespaCLI-Error")
84	        print("::error::Errors reported by VespaCLI:")
85	        print(process.stderr.decode('utf-8'))
86	        print("::endgroup::")
87	
88	    if process.returncode != 0:
89	        print("::error::Errors encountered while feeding Vespa application.")
90	        sys.exit(process.returncode)
91	
92	    return process.stdout.decode('utf-8')
93	
94	
95	def get_docs(index):
96	    file = open(index, "r", encoding='utf-8')
97	    return json.load(file)
98	
99	
100	def get_indexed_docids(endpoint, namespace, doc_type):
101	    docids = set()
102	    continuation = ""
103	    while continuation is not None:
104	        json = vespa_visit(endpoint, namespace, doc_type, continuation)
105	        documents = find(json, "documents")
106	        if documents is not None:
107	            ids = [ find(document, "id") for document in documents ]
108	            for id in ids:
109	                # The document id might contain chars that needs to be escaped for the delete/put operation to work
110	                # also for comparison with what is in the feed
111	                docid = get_document_id(id) # return the last part
112	                encoded = urllib.parse.quote(docid) #escape
113	                id = id.replace(docid, encoded)
114	                docids.add(id)
115	        continuation = find(json, "continuation")
116	    return docids
117	
118	
119	def get_feed_docids(feed, namespace, doc_type):
120	    with open(feed, "r", encoding='utf-8') as f:
121	        feed_json = json.load(f)
122	    if doc_type == "doc":
123	        return set(["id:{0}:doc::".format(namespace) + find(doc, "fields.namespace") + find(doc, "fields.path") for doc in feed_json])
124	    elif doc_type == "term":
125	        return set(["id:{0}:term::".format(namespace) + str(find(doc, "fields.hash")) for doc in feed_json])
126	    elif doc_type == "paragraph":
127	        return set([doc['put'] for doc in feed_json])

129	
130	def print_header(msg):
131	    print("")
132	    print("*" * 80)
133	    print("* {0}".format(msg))
134	    print("*" * 80)

136	
137	def read_config(config_file):
138	    with open(config_file, "r") as f:
139	        return yaml.safe_load(f)
140	
141	
142	def update_endpoint(endpoint, config):
143	    do_remove_index = config["search"]["do_index_removal_before_feed"]
144	    do_feed = config["search"]["do_feed"]
145	    namespace = config["search"]["namespace"]
146	    doc_type = config["search"]["doc_type"]
147	
148	    endpoint_url = endpoint["url"]
149	    endpoint_url = endpoint_url[:-1] if endpoint_url.endswith("/") else endpoint_url
150	    endpoint_indexes = endpoint["indexes"]
151	
152	    print_header("Retrieving already indexed document ids for endpoint {0}".format(endpoint_url))
153	    docids_in_index = get_indexed_docids(endpoint_url, namespace, doc_type)
154	    print("{0} documents found.".format(len(docids_in_index)))
155	
156	    if do_remove_index:
157	        print_header("Removing all indexed documents in {0}".format(endpoint_url))
158	        vespa_remove(endpoint_url, docids_in_index, namespace, doc_type)
159	        print("{0} documents removed.".format(len(docids_in_index)))
160	
161	    if do_feed:
162	        docids_in_feed = set()
163	        print_header("Parsing feed file(s) for document ids")
164	        for index in endpoint_indexes:
165	            assert os.path.exists(index)
166	            docids_in_feed = docids_in_feed.union(get_feed_docids(index, namespace, doc_type))
167	        print("{0} documents found.".format(len(docids_in_feed)))
168	
169	        if len(docids_in_feed) == 0:
170	            return
171	
172	        docids_to_remove = docids_in_index.difference(docids_in_feed)
173	        if len(docids_to_remove) > 0:
174	            print_header("Removing indexed documents not in feed in {0}".format(endpoint_url))
175	            for id in docids_to_remove:
176	                print("To Remove: {0}".format(id))
177	            vespa_remove(endpoint_url, docids_to_remove, namespace, doc_type)
178	            print("{0} documents removed.".format(len(docids_to_remove)))
179	        else:
180	            print("No documents to be removed.")
181	
182	        for index in endpoint_indexes:
183	            print_header("Feeding {0} to {1}...".format(index, endpoint_url))
184	            print(vespa_feed(endpoint_url, index, namespace, doc_type))
185	
186	        print("{0} documents fed.".format(len(docids_in_feed)))
187	
188	
189	def main():
190	    configuration_file = sys.argv[1]
191	    config = read_config(configuration_file)
192	    global session
193	    session = requests.Session()
194	    retries = Retry(total=10, connect=10,
195	        backoff_factor=0.8,
196	        status_forcelist=[ 500, 503, 504, 429 ]
197	    )
198	    session.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(max_retries=retries))
199	    session.cert = (get_public_cert_path(), get_private_key_path())
200	    for endpoint in config["search"]["feed_endpoints"]:
201	        update_endpoint(endpoint, config)
202	
203

1	# The taxonomy, in full
2	
3	An **energy smell** is code that spends energy on work the program does not
4	need, and that a specific refactoring can remove without changing what the
5	program does. This taxonomy names them: twelve categories, sixty-five root
6	causes.
7	
8	This page is what to look for in step 1. Read it before you read the code, and
9	keep it beside you: of every function, ask whether any of these is happening
10	there. The **category table** says what each family of waste covers; the
11	**root cause table** below it lists all sixty-five, one line each — enough to
12	recognise one, not enough to decide it. Deciding is step 2, with the root
13	cause's card.
14	
15	Cards live at `reference/categories/<ID>.md` — a category's root causes, with
16	the repair for each — and `reference/root-causes/<ID>.<S>.md`, which open at
17	`step.py done 1`.
18	
19	## Categories
20	
21	| ID | Category | Covers | Card |
22	|---|---|---|---|
23	| **C1** | Redundant Computation | Energy waste from executing work that does not contribute to the program's required output or that leaves program state unchanged | `reference/categories/C1.md` (8) |
24	| **C2** | Unnecessary Call Overhead | Energy waste from extra layers of function calls, method delegation, or dynamic dispatch that add overhead without proportional benefit | `reference/categories/C2.md` (3) |
25	| **C3** | Inefficient Iteration Patterns | Energy waste from loops that perform more per-iteration work than necessary, iterate more times than required, use suboptimal loop constructs, or fail to terminate correctly | `reference/categories/C3.md` (7) |
26	| **C4** | Inefficient Control Flow | Energy waste from branching, conditions, or dispatch logic that performs unnecessary checks, uses suboptimal evaluation order, or employs patterns that prevent interpreter optimization | `reference/categories/C4.md` (8) |
27	| **C5** | Suboptimal Data Structures | Energy waste from choosing, provisioning, or converting data structures that do not match the workload's access pattern or size requirements | `reference/categories/C5.md` (4) |
28	| **C6** | Unnecessary Memory Usage | Patterns that allocate, copy, retain, or leak memory beyond what the workload requires, increasing garbage collection overhead, memory-bus traffic, and system energy consumption | `reference/categories/C6.md` (7) |
29	| **C7** | Suboptimal Algorithmic | Energy waste from choosing an algorithm, decomposition, or computation strategy that explores more of the problem space than necessary or uses higher complexity than the problem requires | `reference/categories/C7.md` (5) |
30	| **C8** | Missing Reuse | Energy waste from failing to store and reuse results of expensive computations, lookups, or data fetches, causing the same work to be repeated across calls, requests, or access sites | `reference/categories/C8.md` (4) |
31	| **C9** | Inefficient External Data Access | Energy waste from inefficient interaction with external systems: databases, file systems, network services, and APIs | `reference/categories/C9.md` (4) |
32	| **C10** | Underused Language Primitives | Energy waste from not using available optimized language features, standard library functions, or runtime-specific constructs that would accomplish the same task more efficiently | `reference/categories/C10.md` (6) |
33	| **C11** | Inefficient Concurrency Management | Energy waste from thread/task misuse, synchronization overhead, contention, or failure to exploit available parallelism | `reference/categories/C11.md` (5) |
34	| **C12** | Poor Hardware Locality Usage | Energy waste driven by CPU and memory hierarchy behavior such as cache misses, branch misprediction, and suboptimal memory access patterns | `reference/categories/C12.md` (4) |
35	
36	## Every root cause, one line each
37	
38	### C1 — Redundant Computation
39	
40	| ID | Name | Looks for |
41	|---|---|---|
42	| **C1.S1** | Dead Code | a value computed and bound to a name that nothing ever reads |
43	| **C1.S2** | Redundant Assignment | a store that leaves the program's state exactly as it already was |
44	| **C1.S3** | Redundant Control Flow | a branch whose outcome is the same whichever way it goes |
45	| **C1.S4** | Repeated Computation | the same value computed twice in one scope, where one local would serve both |
46	| **C1.S5** | Resultless Computation | a computation run in full whose result nothing downstream actually needs |
47	| **C1.S6** | Unnecessary Initialization | setup done unconditionally that only one path actually needs |
48	| **C1.S7** | Unnecessary Variable | a name bound, read exactly once, and never needed again |
49	| **C1.S8** | Excessive Runtime-Management Calls | runtime housekeeping invoked far more often than anything needs it |
50	
51	### C2 — Unnecessary Call Overhead
52	
53	| ID | Name | Looks for |
54	|---|---|---|
55	| **C2.S1** | Unnecessary Method Delegation | a wrapper or property that forwards, adds nothing, and sits on a hot path |
56	| **C2.S2** | Missing Static Declaration | a method that never touches `self` and still pays to be bound to an instance |
57	| **C2.S3** | Excessive Modularization in Hot Path | a chain of thin layers whose frames cost more than the work at the bottom |
58	
59	### C3 — Inefficient Iteration Patterns
60	
61	| ID | Name | Looks for |
62	|---|---|---|
63	| **C3.S1** | Inefficient Iteration Construct | a loop written in a form that does more interpreter work per element than it needs to |
64	| **C3.S2** | Recomputing Loop-Invariant Values | an expression recomputed every iteration whose answer never changes |
65	| **C3.S3** | Inefficient Per-Iteration Setup | an object or resource created once per iteration that the whole loop could share |
66	| **C3.S4** | Inefficient Nested Iteration | an inner loop that searches, where a lookup would turn n*m into n+m |
67	| **C3.S5** | Missing Loop Early Exit | a loop that keeps going after its answer is already settled |
68	| **C3.S6** | Unfiltered Bulk Iteration | the whole collection processed when only a subset was ever wanted |
69	| **C3.S7** | Inefficient Array Mutation in Loop | a collection edited while it is being walked |
70	
71	### C4 — Inefficient Control Flow
72	
73	| ID | Name | Looks for |
74	|---|---|---|
75	| **C4.S1** | Poor Short-Circuit Ordering | a boolean chain that evaluates its expensive operand before the cheap one that usually decides |
76	| **C4.S2** | Redundant Conditional Evaluation | a test whose answer was already settled before it ran |
77	| **C4.S3** | Inefficient Conditional Nesting | a nest or chain of branches that tests more than it has to, where a lookup would test once |
78	| **C4.S4** | Missing Else-If | consecutive `if`s on one subject that are exclusive in fact but not in form |
79	| **C4.S5** | Expensive Comparison | a type check made per element where the answer never varies or the types could dispatch themselves |
80	| **C4.S6** | Expensive Exception Control Flow | an exception used as ordinary control flow, on a path where it is raised often |
81	| **C4.S7** | Missing Edge-Case Guards | a missing cheap test that would let a common trivial input skip the expensive path |
82	| **C4.S8** | Non-Idiomatic Condition | a condition spelled the long way round, missing the interpreter's fast path |
83	
84	### C5 — Suboptimal Data Structures
85	
86	| ID | Name | Looks for |
87	|---|---|---|
88	| **C5.S1** | Inefficient Data Structure Choice | a container whose type makes its most frequent operation the expensive one |
89	| **C5.S2** | Missing Helper Type | a collection searched again and again where one index built beside it would answer every question |
90	| **C5.S3** | Over-Provisioned Data Type | a representation heavier than the data it holds actually requires |
91	| **C5.S4** | Unnecessary Representation Change | a conversion between representations that the code on either side did not need |
92	
93	### C6 — Unnecessary Memory Usage
94	
95	| ID | Name | Looks for |
96	|---|---|---|
97	| **C6.S1** | Unnecessary Object | objects created and thrown away that never needed to exist |
98	| **C6.S2** | Unnecessary Copying | data duplicated when the original could have been used or changed in place |
99	| **C6.S3** | Unnecessary Data Materialization | a whole sequence built in memory when the consumer wanted it one element at a time |
100	| **C6.S4** | Oversized Data Retaining | something long-lived holding far more data than anything later reads |
101	| **C6.S5** | Over-Allocation | capacity reserved up front for data that never arrives |
102	| **C6.S6** | Leaked Resource Handles | a file, socket or connection acquired with nothing guaranteeing its release |
103	| **C6.S7** | Leaking Mutable Default Arguments | a mutable default argument that quietly accumulates across every call |
104	
105	### C7 — Suboptimal Algorithmic
106	
107	| ID | Name | Looks for |
108	|---|---|---|
109	| **C7.S1** | Suboptimal Algorithm Choice | an algorithm of worse complexity than the problem requires |
110	| **C7.S2** | Inefficient Problem Decomposition | a search exploring subproblems it could have pruned, reordered or reused |
111	| **C7.S3** | Avoidable Recursive Implementation | a recursion paying a frame per level where a loop would use one |
112	| **C7.S4** | Inefficient Operation Ordering | two commuting operations in the order that makes the expensive one see more data |
113	| **C7.S5** | Unsimplified Operation | an operation doing more work than an algebraic fact about its inputs requires |
114	
115	### C8 — Missing Reuse
116	
117	| ID | Name | Looks for |
118	|---|---|---|
119	| **C8.S1** | Missing Memoization Cache | a deterministic computation repeated across calls that a cache would answer |
120	| **C8.S2** | Missing Derived-Value Reuse | an expensive artefact derived again on every use instead of once for the process |
121	| **C8.S3** | Missing Local Lookup Caching | a name or attribute chain re-resolved every iteration for a value that never moves |
122	| **C8.S4** | Redundant Data Fetching | the same external data fetched again when the copy in memory was still good |
123	
124	### C9 — Inefficient External Data Access
125	
126	| ID | Name | Looks for |
127	|---|---|---|
128	| **C9.S1** | Fragmented I/O Calls | many small independent external operations where one bulk operation would do |
129	| **C9.S2** | Oversized Data Retrieval | more data pulled across a process boundary than the program ever consults |
130	| **C9.S3** | Inefficient Retrieval Paths | one fetch per row of an earlier fetch, where a join would have taken one trip |
131	| **C9.S4** | Expensive Query Pattern | a query whose shape makes the engine do far more work than the answer needs |
132	
133	### C10 — Underused Language Primitives
134	
135	| ID | Name | Looks for |
136	|---|---|---|
137	| **C10.S1** | Skipping Optimized Built-ins | a hand-written loop doing bulk work a C-level primitive already does |
138	| **C10.S2** | Inefficient Built-in Choice | one primitive used where a cheaper primitive computes the same answer |
139	| **C10.S3** | Missing Bulk Primitive Usage | a per-element call inside a loop that a single batched call would replace |
140	| **C10.S4** | Inefficient String Concatenation | a string grown with `+=` in a loop, where the target is aliased or the parts are many |
141	| **C10.S5** | Inefficient Scope Lookup | a global or builtin re-resolved through the module namespace on every iteration |
142	| **C10.S6** | Expensive Operator Overloads | an operator on a user-defined type dispatching and allocating once per element |
143	
144	### C11 — Inefficient Concurrency Management
145	
146	| ID | Name | Looks for |
147	|---|---|---|
148	| **C11.S1** | Excessive Lock Contention | a lock held across work that shares nothing, serialising what could overlap |
149	| **C11.S2** | Forced Serial Bottleneck | concurrency paid for in full while one shared resource serialises all of it |
150	| **C11.S3** | Leaked Background Threads | workers started and never stopped, accumulating for the life of the process |
151	| **C11.S4** | Blocking The Main Thread | a synchronous blocking call inside a coroutine, stopping every other task |
152	| **C11.S5** | Missed Parallelism Opportunities | independent work run one item at a time when the waits could have overlapped |
153	
154	### C12 — Poor Hardware Locality Usage
155	
156	| ID | Name | Looks for |
157	|---|---|---|
158	| **C12.S1** | Inefficient Large-Stride Traversal | a contiguous buffer traversed against the direction its memory is laid out in |
159	| **C12.S2** | Sparse Element Access | scattered reads into a large buffer, using one element of every cache line fetched |
160	| **C12.S3** | Unpredictable Branches | a data-dependent branch in a compiled hot loop that the CPU cannot predict |
161	| **C12.S4** | Inefficient Array Declaration Order | a declared struct whose field order puts cold data in front of hot data |
162	
163	## Using this well
164	
165	**Any category may apply to any code.** Nothing about a repository rules a
166	category in or out in advance. Work from what the code actually does.
167	
168	**Read the card, not the name, and not the line above.** These names are three
169	or four words long and several of them cover something narrower — or wider —
170	than they sound like. The one-line summaries here are index entries, precise
171	enough to recognise something by and not enough to decide anything from. The
172	card is the claim.
173	
174	**The index tells you what to look for, not what you will find.** A unit goes
175	on your list because of what its code does, not because a line here sounds
176	like it. Finding nothing in a category is a perfectly ordinary outcome.
177	
178	**Cards overlap.** When two root causes both describe what you repaired,
179	either attribution is fine — say which you chose.
180	
181	## What tools can and cannot contribute
182	
183	Any static rule, in any tool, recognises a syntactic shape that somebody
184	described in advance. That makes rules dependable about the shapes they know
185	and completely blind to everything else. Two consequences, and they point in
186	opposite directions:
187	
188	- **A rule firing has observed a pattern, not diagnosed a problem.** Every
189	  pattern in this taxonomy is the right thing to write somewhere, which is what
190	  each card's `Looks like it, but is not` section records.
191	  Some of what any rule reports is therefore wrong here, and saying which is
192	  part of the job.
193	- **A rule staying quiet has observed nothing.** Waste that lives in the
194	  arrangement of a program — work computed and discarded, a data shape that
195	  forces every later step to compensate, a query issued once per row — has no
196	  fixed syntactic shape at all, and is usually the expensive kind.
197	
198	Reading the code is the primary method here. Anything a tool tells you is a
199	second opinion to reconcile with what you already worked out.
200

11	def get_result(query_vector):
12

14	    'hits': args.hits,

25	    return 0, 0, []
26	
27	  result = response.json()
28	  time = result['timing']['searchtime']*1000
29	  total_hits = result['root']['fields']['totalCount']
30	  docs = []
31	  for h in result['root']['children']:
32	    fields = h.get('fields',None)
33	    docs.append(fields.get('id'))
34	  return time,total_hits,docs
35	 
36	def read_queries():
37	  with open(args.query_file, 'rb') as fq:
38	    q_count = struct.unpack('i', fq.read(4))[0]
39	    q_dimension = struct.unpack('i', fq.read(4))[0]
40	    queries = np.frombuffer(fq.read(q_count * q_dimension), dtype=np.int8).reshape((q_count, q_dimension))
41	    return queries
42	
43	def knn_result_read():
44	  n, d = map(int, np.fromfile(args.query_gt_file, dtype="uint32", count=2))
45	  assert os.stat(args.query_gt_file).st_size == 8 + n * d * (4 + 4)
46	  f = open(args.query_gt_file, "rb")
47	  f.seek(4+4)
48	  I = np.fromfile(f, dtype="int32", count=n * d).reshape(n, d)
49	  D = np.fromfile(f, dtype="float32", count=n * d).reshape(n, d)
50	  return I, D
51	
52	def compute_recall_with_distance_ties(true_ids, true_dists, run_ids, count):
53	  # From https://github.com/harsha-simhadri/big-ann-benchmarks/blob/main/benchmark/plotting/metrics.py#L15
54	  # This function assumes "true_dists" is monotonic either increasing or decreasing
55	  found_tie = False
56	  gt_size = np.shape(true_dists)[0]
57	  if gt_size==count:
58	  # nothing fancy to do in this case
59	    recall =  len(set(true_ids[:count]) & set(run_ids))
60	  else:
61	    dist_tie_check = true_dists[count-1] # tie check anchored at count-1 in GT dists
62	    set_end = gt_size
63	    for i in range(count, gt_size):
64	      is_close = abs(dist_tie_check - true_dists[i] ) < 1e-6 
65	      if not is_close:
66	        set_end = i
67	        break
68	
69	    found_tie = set_end > count
70	    recall =  len(set(true_ids[:set_end]) & set(run_ids))
71	 
72	  return recall, found_tie
73	
74	
75	def main():
76	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
77	    parser.add_argument("--endpoint", type=str, required=True) 
78	    parser.add_argument("--query_file", type=str, required=True)
79	    parser.add_argument("--query_gt_file", type=str, required=True)

83	    parser.add_argument("--rank_count", type=int, default=1000)
84	    parser.add_argument("--distance_prune_threshold", type=float, default=0.80)
85	    parser.add_argument("--certificate", type=str)
86	    parser.add_argument("--key", type=str)
87	    parser.add_argument("--queries", type=int, default=0)
88	
89	    global args
90	    args = parser.parse_args()
91	
92	    queries = read_queries()
93	    truths,distances =  knn_result_read() 
94	    recalls = []
95	    times = []
96	    hits = []
97	
98	    global session
99	    session = requests.Session()
100	    if args.certificate and args.key:
101	      session.cert = (args.certificate, args.key)
102	    if args.queries != 0:
103	        queries = queries[0:args.queries]
104	    for i in tqdm(range(0,len(queries))):
105	      query = queries[i]
106	      time,total_hits,result = get_result(query)
107	      times.append(time)
108	      hits.append(total_hits)
109	      recall_10,found_tie =  compute_recall_with_distance_ties(truths[i], distances[i], result, 10) 
110	      recalls.append(10*recall_10)
111	    print("{},{}".format(np.average(recalls), np.average(times)))
112

115	    main()

5	import torch
6	from transformers import AutoModel, BertPreTrainedModel
7	
8	
9	class VespaColBERT(BertPreTrainedModel):
10	    """ A wrapper around the Hugging Face Transformers model to export to ONNX
11	    for inference with Vespa colbert-embedder.
12	    https://docs.vespa.ai/en/embedding.html#colbert-embedder
13	    """
14	    def __init__(self, config, dim):
15	        super().__init__(config)
16	        self.bert = AutoModel.from_config(config)
17	        self.linear = torch.nn.Linear(config.hidden_size, dim, bias=False)
18	        self.init_weights()
19	
20	    def forward(self, input_ids, attention_mask):
21	        Q = self.bert(input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask)[0]
22	        # Projection layer 
23	        Q = self.linear(Q)
24	        # Normalization so that each vector is unit length 
25	        return torch.nn.functional.normalize(Q, p=2, dim=2)
26	
27	
28	# Replace with your model trained with ColBERT
29	
30	import argparse
31	parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
32	parser.add_argument("--hf_model", type=str, default='answerdotai/answerai-colbert-small-v1') 
33	parser.add_argument("--dims", type=int, default=96)
34	parser.add_argument("--out_file", type=str, default="model.onnx")

36	
37	print("Vespa ONNX export for model " + args.hf_model + " with dims " + str(args.dims) + " to " + args.out_file)

11	import argparse
12	from typing import Any, Dict
13	import pandas as pd
14	
15	from vespa.application import Vespa
16	from vespa.evaluation import VespaEvaluator
17	
18	
19	def main():
20	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
21	    parser.add_argument(
22	        "--endpoint",
23	        type=str,
24	        required=True,
25	        help="Vespa endpoint, e.g. http://localhost",
26	    )
27	    parser.add_argument(
28	        "--port", type=int, default=8080, help="Vespa port (default: 8080)"
29	    )
30	    parser.add_argument(
31	        "--ranking", type=str, required=True, help="Ranking profile to use"
32	    )
33	    parser.add_argument(
34	        "--example_file", type=str, required=True, help="Path to example parquet file"
35	    )
36	    parser.add_argument(
37	        "--qrel_file", type=str, required=True, help="Path to qrel file"
38	    )
39	    parser.add_argument(
40	        "--hits", type=int, default=400, help="Number of hits to return"
41	    )
42	    parser.add_argument(
43	        "--certificate", type=str, help="Path to SSL certificate (optional)"
44	    )
45	    parser.add_argument("--key", type=str, help="Path to SSL key (optional)")
46	    args = parser.parse_args()
47	    print(args)
48	
49	    # ----------------------
50	    # Load and process examples
51	    # ----------------------
52	    df = pd.read_parquet(args.example_file)
53	    df = df[df["split"] == "test"]
54	    df = df[df["product_locale"] == "us"]
55	    df = df[df["small_version"] == 1]
56	
57	    # Group by query_id to aggregate the query text and build the recall string
58	    grouped_df = (
59	        df.groupby("query_id")
60	        .agg(
61	            {
62	                "query": "first",
63	                "product_id": lambda ids: "+({})".format(
64	                    " ".join("id:{}".format(pid) for pid in ids)
65	                ),
66	            }
67	        )
68	        .reset_index()
69	        .rename(columns={"product_id": "recall"})
70	    )
71	    # Ensure query IDs are strings
72	    grouped_df["query_id"] = grouped_df["query_id"].astype(str)
73	
74	    # Create dictionaries mapping query_id -> query text and query_id -> recall string
75	    query_dict = grouped_df.set_index("query_id")["query"].to_dict()
76	    qid_to_recall_str = grouped_df.set_index("query_id")["recall"].to_dict()
77	
78	    # ----------------------
79	    # Load qrels from the Vespa Cloud sample
80	    # ----------------------
81	    df_qrels = pd.read_csv(
82	        args.qrel_file,
83	        sep=" ",
84	        header=None,
85	    )
86	    df_qrels.columns = ["query_id", "Q0", "product_id", "relevance"]
87	    # Mapping as in the pyvespa example: 1 -> 0, 2 -> 0.01, 3 -> 0.1, 4 -> 1
88	    esci_mapping = {1: 0, 2: 0.01, 3: 0.1, 4: 1}
89	    df_qrels["relevance"] = df_qrels["relevance"].map(esci_mapping)
90	    df_qrels["query_id"] = df_qrels["query_id"].astype(str)
91	    grouped_qrels = (
92	        df_qrels.groupby("query_id")
93	        .apply(lambda group: dict(zip(group["product_id"], group["relevance"])), include_groups=False)
94	        .to_dict()
95	    )
96	
97	    # Only use queries that have associated qrels
98	    common_query_ids = set(query_dict.keys()) & set(grouped_qrels.keys())
99	    if not common_query_ids:
100	        print("No common query IDs found between examples and qrels.")
101	        return
102	
103	    filtered_queries = {qid: query_dict[qid] for qid in common_query_ids}
104	    filtered_qrels = {qid: grouped_qrels[qid] for qid in common_query_ids}
105	
106	    # ----------------------
107	    # Define the Vespa query function
108	    # ----------------------
109	    def vespa_query_fn(query_text: str, top_k: int, query_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
110	        """
111	        Given a query text and query_id, return a Vespa query request body.
112	        The ranking profile and number of hits are provided as command-line arguments.
113	        The recall string is built from the qid_to_recall_str mapping.
114	        """
115	        return {
116	            "yql": (
117	                "select id from product where userQuery() or "
118	                "({targetHits:100}nearestNeighbor(title_embedding, q_title)) or "
119	                "({targetHits:100}nearestNeighbor(description_embedding, q_description))"
120	            ),
121	            "query": query_text,
122	            "input.query(q_title)": f'embed(title, "{query_text}")',
123	            "input.query(q_description)": f'embed(description, "{query_text}")',
124	            "input.query(query_tokens)": f'embed(tokenizer, "{query_text}")',
125	            "ranking": args.ranking,
126	            "hits": args.hits,
127	            "timeout": "15s",
128	            "recall": qid_to_recall_str[query_id],
129	            "ranking.softtimeout.enable": "false",
130	        }
131	
132	    # ----------------------
133	    # Initialize the Vespa application using the provided endpoint and session
134	    # ----------------------
135	    # Note: The endpoint is expected to be something like "http://localhost"
136	    app = Vespa(args.endpoint, port=args.port, key=args.key, cert=args.certificate)
137	
138	    # ----------------------
139	    # Create and run the evaluator
140	    # ----------------------
141	    # For evaluation, we set ndcg_at_k to the maximum number of relevant documents among all queries.
142	    ndcg_at_k_value = max(len(rels) for rels in filtered_qrels.values())
143	    evaluator = VespaEvaluator(
144	        queries=filtered_queries,
145	        relevant_docs=filtered_qrels,
146	        vespa_query_fn=vespa_query_fn,
147	        app=app,
148	        ndcg_at_k=[ndcg_at_k_value],
149	    )
150	
151	    results = evaluator.run()
152	
153	    # ----------------------
154	    # Output the evaluation results
155	    # ----------------------
156	    print("Evaluation results:")
157	    print(results)
158	
159	
160	if __name__ == "__main__":
161	    main()

25	overlay_scrollbars_manager = Script(

28	        const { OverlayScrollbars } = OverlayScrollbarsGlobal;
29	
30	        function getPreferredTheme() {
31	            return localStorage.theme === 'dark' || (!('theme' in localStorage) && window.matchMedia('(prefers-color-scheme: dark)').matches)
32	                ? 'dark'
33	                : 'light';

36	        function applyOverlayScrollbars(element, scrollbarTheme) {
37	            // Destroy existing OverlayScrollbars instance if it exists
38	            const instance = OverlayScrollbars(element);
39	            if (instance) {
40	                instance.destroy();
41	            }
42	
43	            // Reinitialize OverlayScrollbars with the correct theme and settings
44	            OverlayScrollbars(element, {
45	                overflow: {

55	            });
56	        }
57	
58	        // Function to get the current scrollbar theme (light or dark)
59	        function getScrollbarTheme() {
60	            const isDarkMode = getPreferredTheme() === 'dark';
61	            return isDarkMode ? 'os-theme-light' : 'os-theme-dark';  // Light theme in dark mode, dark theme in light mode
62	        }
63	
64	        // Expose the common functions globally for reuse
65	        window.OverlayScrollbarsManager = {

8	def create_conditions(conditions_list):
9	    """Convert an array of condition strings into Vespa QueryBuilder conditions."""
10	
11	    # Define supported operators
12	    operators = {
13	        ">": lambda f, v: f > v,
14	        "<": lambda f, v: f < v,
15	        "=": lambda f, v: f == v,
16	        "!=": lambda f, v: f != v,
17	        ">=": lambda f, v: f >= v,
18	        "<=": lambda f, v: f <= v,
19	        "contains": lambda f, v: f.contains(v),  # Special case for text search
20	    }
21	
22	    parsed_conditions = []
23	
24	    for condition_str in conditions_list:
25	        parts = condition_str.split(
26	            " ", 2
27	        )  # Split into max 3 parts to handle "contains" operator properly
28	
29	        if len(parts) < 3:
30	            raise ValueError(
31	                f"Invalid condition format: '{condition_str}'. Expected format: 'field operator value'"
32	            )
33	
34	        field, operator, value = parts[0], parts[1], parts[2]
35	
36	        # Convert numeric values if applicable
37	        try:
38	            value = float(value) if "." in value or value.isdigit() else value
39	        except ValueError:
40	            pass  # Keep as string if conversion fails
41	
42	        # Validate operator
43	        if operator not in operators:
44	            raise ValueError(
45	                f"Unsupported operator: '{operator}' in condition '{condition_str}'"
46	            )
47	
48	        # Create QueryField object and apply operator function
49	        query_field = qf(field)
50	        parsed_conditions.append(operators[operator](query_field, value))
51	
52	    return parsed_conditions  # Returns a list of Condition objects

11	def find(json, path, separator = "."):
12	    if len(path) == 0: return json
13	    head, _, rest = path.partition(separator)
14	    return find(json[head], rest) if head in json else None
15

22	def call(args):
23	    proc = subprocess.Popen(args, stdout=subprocess.PIPE)
24	    (out, err) = proc.communicate()
25	    return out
26	
27	def vespa_get(endpoint, operation, options):
28	    endpoint = endpoint[:-1] if endpoint.endswith("/") else endpoint
29	    url = "{0}/{1}?{2}".format(endpoint, operation, "&".join(options))
30	    print(url)
31	    return call([
32	        "curl",
33	        "-gsS",
34	        url ])
35	
36	
37	def vespa_delete(endpoint, operation, options):
38	    endpoint = endpoint[:-1] if endpoint.endswith("/") else endpoint
39	    url = "{0}/{1}?{2}".format(endpoint, operation, "&".join(options))
40	    return call([
41	        "curl",
42	        "-gsS",
43	        "-X", "DELETE",
44	        url
45	    ])
46	
47	
48	def vespa_post(endpoint, doc, docid, namespace):
49	    endpoint = endpoint[:-1] if endpoint.endswith("/") else endpoint
50	    url = "{0}/document/v1/{1}/doc/docid/{2}".format(endpoint, namespace, docid)
51	    return call([
52	        "curl",
53	        "-sS",
54	        "-H", "Content-Type:application/json",
55	        "-X", "POST",
56	        "--data-binary", "{0}".format(doc),
57	        url
58	    ])
59	
60	
61	def vespa_visit(endpoint, namespace, continuation = None):
62	    options = []
63	    options.append("wantedDocumentCount=500")
64	    if continuation is not None and len(continuation) > 0:
65	        options.append("&continuation={0}".format(continuation))
66	    response = vespa_get(endpoint, "document/v1/{0}/doc/docid".format(namespace), options)
67	    try:
68	        return json.loads(response)
69	    except:
70	        print("Unable to parse JSON response from {0}. Should not happen, endpoint down? response: {1}".format(endpoint, response))
71	        sys.exit(1)
72	    return {}

75	def vespa_remove(endpoint, doc_ids, namespace):

95	    docids = set()
96	    continuation = ""
97	    while continuation is not None:

99	        documents = find(json, "documents")

109	def get_feed_docids(feed, namespace):

122	def read_config():

124	        return yaml.safe_load(f)

126	
127	def update_endpoint(endpoint, config):
128	    do_remove_index = config["search"]["do_index_removal_before_feed"]
129	    do_feed = config["search"]["do_feed"]
130	    namespace = config["search"]["namespace"]
131	
132	    endpoint_url = endpoint["url"]
133	    endpoint_indexes = endpoint["indexes"]
134	
135	    print_header("Retrieving already indexed document ids for endpoint {0}".format(endpoint_url))
136	    docids_in_index = get_indexed_docids(endpoint_url, namespace)
137	    print("{0} documents found.".format(len(docids_in_index)))
138	
139	    if do_remove_index:
140	        print_header("Removing all indexed documents in {0}".format(endpoint_url))
141	        vespa_remove(endpoint_url, docids_in_index, namespace)
142	        print("{0} documents removed.".format(len(docids_in_index)))
143	
144	    if do_feed:
145	        docids_in_feed = set()
146	        print_header("Parsing feed file(s) for document ids")
147	        for index in endpoint_indexes:
148	            assert os.path.exists(index)
149	            docids_in_feed = docids_in_feed.union(get_feed_docids(index, namespace))
150	        print("{0} documents found.".format(len(docids_in_feed)))
151	
152	        if len(docids_in_feed) == 0:
153	            return
154	
155	        docids_to_remove = docids_in_index.difference(docids_in_feed)
156	        if len(docids_to_remove) > 0:
157	            print_header("Removing indexed documents not in feed in {0}".format(endpoint_url))
158	            for id in docids_to_remove:
159	                print("To Remove: {0}".format(id))
160	            vespa_remove(endpoint_url, docids_to_remove, namespace)
161	            print("{0} documents removed.".format(len(docids_to_remove)))
162	        else:
163	            print("No documents to be removed.")
164	
165	        for index in endpoint_indexes:
166	            print_header("Feeding {0} to {1}...".format(index, endpoint_url))
167	            print(vespa_feed(endpoint_url, index, namespace))
168	
169	        print("{0} documents fed.".format(len(docids_in_feed)))
170	
171	
172	def main():
173	    config = read_config()
174	    for endpoint in config["search"]["feed_endpoints"]:
175	        update_endpoint(endpoint, config)

177	
178	if __name__ == "__main__":
179	    main()

1	import sys
2	import re
3	import json
4	
5	
6	def read_json_file(file_path):
7	    data = None
8	    with open(file_path, "r") as f:
9	        data = json.load(f)
10	    return data
11	
12	def get_phrases(terms):
13	    # from "learning to rank" to ['learning to rank', 'to rank', 'rank']
14	    phrases = []
15	    phrases.append(terms)
16	    end = terms.find(' ')
17	    while end != -1:
18	        start = end+1
19	        remainder = terms[start:]
20	        phrases.append(remainder)
21	        end = terms.find(' ', start)
22	    return phrases
23	
24	def write_json_file(terms, file_path):
25	    feed_list = [
26	        {
27	            "update": f'id:term:term::{re.sub(r" ", "/", term)}',
28	            "create": True,
29	            "fields": {
30	                "term": {"assign": data["term"]},
31	                "terms": {"assign": get_phrases(data["term"])},
32	                "corpus_count": {"assign": data["count"]},
33	                "document_count": {"assign": data["docs"]},
34	            },
35	        }
36	        for (term, data) in terms.items()
37	    ]
38	    with open(file_path, "w") as f:
39	        json.dump(feed_list, f, indent=2)
40	
41	
42	def read_common_words(file_path):
43	    common_words = set()
44	    with open(file_path, "r") as f:
45	        lines = f.readlines()
46	        for line in lines:
47	            common_words.add(line.strip())
48	    return common_words
49	
50	
51	def clean_text(text):
52	    return re.split(r"[^a-z0-9]+", text.lower())
53	
54	
55	def count_terms(doc, term_length=1, common_words=set()):
56	    counts = {}
57	    for win_len in range(1, term_length + 1):
58	        for i in range(len(doc) + 1 - win_len):
59	            if not any(
60	                map(lambda word: word in common_words, doc[i : i + win_len])
61	            ):
62	                term = " ".join(doc[i : i + win_len])
63	                if  len(term) > 0 and not term.isspace():
64	                    counts[term] = counts.get(term, 0) + 1
65	    return counts
66	
67	
68	def process_doc(doc_fields, term_length=1, common_words=set()):
69	    if doc_fields["title"] and doc_fields["content"]:
70	        title_counts = count_terms(
71	            clean_text(doc_fields["title"]), term_length, common_words
72	        )
73	        content_counts = count_terms(
74	            clean_text(doc_fields["content"]), term_length, common_words
75	        )
76	        return {
77	            term: title_counts.get(term, 0) + content_counts.get(term, 0)
78	            for term in list(title_counts.keys()) + list(content_counts.keys())
79	        }
80	    else:
81	        return {}
82	
83	
84	def process_docs(obj, term_length=1, common_words=set()):
85	    doc_counts = [
86	        process_doc(doc["fields"], term_length, common_words) for doc in obj
87	    ]
88	    terms = {}
89	
90	    # Sum counts
91	    for counts in doc_counts:
92	        total_count = sum([count for count in counts.values()])
93	        for (term, count) in counts.items():
94	            if term in terms:
95	                terms[term]["count"] = terms[term]["count"] + count
96	            else:
97	                terms[term] = {"term": term, "count": count}
98	
99	    # Find number of documents containing the term
100	    for term in terms.keys():
101	        terms[term]["docs"] = sum(
102	            [1 if term in doc else 0 for doc in doc_counts]
103	        )
104	
105	    return terms
106	
107	
108	def main():
109	    if len(sys.argv) == 3:
110	        write_json_file(process_docs(read_json_file(sys.argv[1])), sys.argv[2])
111	    elif len(sys.argv) == 4:
112	        write_json_file(
113	            process_docs(read_json_file(sys.argv[1]), int(sys.argv[3])),
114	            sys.argv[2],
115	        )
116	    elif len(sys.argv) == 5:
117	        write_json_file(
118	            process_docs(
119	                read_json_file(sys.argv[1]),
120	                int(sys.argv[3]),
121	                read_common_words(sys.argv[4]),
122	            ),
123	            sys.argv[2],
124	        )
125	    else:

127	            "Wrong number of arguments:",

131	            "outfile.json",
132	            "[number_of_words_in_term [common_words.txt]]",
133	        )
134	
135	
136	if __name__ == "__main__":

1	"""Feed ImageNet-1k into Vespa.
2	
3	Streams ILSVRC/imagenet-1k from HuggingFace, saves JPEGs to IMAGES_DIR,
4	generates DINOv2 embeddings, and feeds to Vespa with bfloat16 tensors.
5	
6	Resumable: skips IDs whose image file is already present on disk.
7	"""
8	from __future__ import annotations
9	
10	import argparse
11	import base64
12	import logging
13	import os
14	from pathlib import Path
15	from typing import Iterable, Iterator
16	
17	import torch
18	from datasets import load_dataset
19	from PIL import Image
20	from transformers import AutoImageProcessor, AutoModel
21	from vespa.application import Vespa
22	
23	logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format="%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(message)s")
24	log = logging.getLogger("feeder")
25	
26	VESPA_URL = os.environ["RIS_VESPA_URL"].rstrip("/")
27	VESPA_CERT_PATH = os.environ.get("RIS_VESPA_CERT_PATH") or None
28	VESPA_KEY_PATH = os.environ.get("RIS_VESPA_KEY_PATH") or None
29	IMAGES_DIR = Path(os.environ.get("RIS_IMAGES_DIR", "/data/images"))
30	MODEL_NAME = os.environ.get("RIS_MODEL_NAME", "facebook/dinov2-base")
31	HF_DATASET = os.environ.get("RIS_HF_DATASET", "ILSVRC/imagenet-1k")
32	BATCH_SIZE = int(os.environ.get("RIS_BATCH_SIZE", "32"))
33	FEED_CONCURRENCY = int(os.environ.get("RIS_FEED_CONCURRENCY", "8"))
34	
35	
36	def _device() -> str:
37	    if torch.cuda.is_available():
38	        return "cuda"
39	    if torch.backends.mps.is_available():
40	        return "mps"
41	    return "cpu"
42	
43	
44	def _save_image(img: Image.Image, path: Path, max_side: int = 1024) -> tuple[int, int]:
45	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
46	    img = img.convert("RGB")
47	    w, h = img.size
48	    if max(w, h) > max_side:
49	        scale = max_side / max(w, h)
50	        img = img.resize((int(w * scale), int(h * scale)), Image.LANCZOS)
51	    img.save(path, format="JPEG", quality=88)
52	    return img.size
53	
54	
55	def _make_id(split: str, index: int) -> str:
56	    return f"{split}-{index:08d}"
57	
58	
59	def _relative_path(split: str, index: int) -> str:
60	    shard = index // 1000
61	    return f"{split}/{shard:04d}/{_make_id(split, index)}.jpg"
62	
63	
64	def _iter_split(split: str, limit: int | None) -> Iterator[tuple[int, dict]]:
65	    log.info("streaming split=%s limit=%s", split, limit)
66	    ds = load_dataset(HF_DATASET, split=split, streaming=True)
67	    for i, ex in enumerate(ds):
68	        if limit is not None and i >= limit:
69	            break
70	        yield i, ex
71	
72	
73	def _batched(iterable: Iterable, size: int) -> Iterator[list]:
74	    batch: list = []
75	    for item in iterable:
76	        batch.append(item)
77	        if len(batch) >= size:
78	            yield batch
79	            batch = []
80	    if batch:
81	        yield batch
82	
83	
84	def _iter_docs_for_feed(docs: list[dict]) -> Iterator[dict]:
85	    for d in docs:
86	        yield {
87	            "id": d["id"],
88	            "fields": {
89	                "id": d["id"],
90	                "filename": d["filename"],
91	                "path": d["path"],
92	                "split": d["split"],
93	                "label": d["label"],
94	                "width": d["width"],
95	                "height": d["height"],
96	                "embedding": {"values": d["embedding"]},
97	                "full_image": d["full_image"],
98	            },
99	        }
100	
101	
102	def run(split: str, limit: int | None, refeed: bool = False) -> None:
103	    device = _device()
104	    log.info("loading %s on %s", MODEL_NAME, device)
105	    processor = AutoImageProcessor.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME)
106	    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(MODEL_NAME).to(device).eval()
107	
108	    vespa_kwargs: dict = {"url": VESPA_URL}
109	    if VESPA_CERT_PATH and VESPA_KEY_PATH:
110	        vespa_kwargs["cert"] = VESPA_CERT_PATH
111	        vespa_kwargs["key"] = VESPA_KEY_PATH
112	    app = Vespa(**vespa_kwargs)
113	
114	    total_ok = 0
115	    total_fail = 0
116	    total_skip = 0
117	
118	    def callback(response, doc_id):
119	        nonlocal total_ok, total_fail
120	        if response.is_successful():
121	            total_ok += 1
122	        else:
123	            total_fail += 1
124	            log.warning("feed fail id=%s status=%s body=%s",
125	                        doc_id, response.get_status_code(), response.get_json())
126	
127	    with torch.inference_mode():
128	        for batch in _batched(_iter_split(split, limit), BATCH_SIZE):
129	            pil_images: list[Image.Image] = []
130	            pending: list[dict] = []
131	
132	            for i, ex in batch:
133	                doc_id = _make_id(split, i)
134	                rel = _relative_path(split, i)
135	                abs_path = IMAGES_DIR / rel
136	                img = ex["image"]
137	                if not isinstance(img, Image.Image):
138	                    continue
139	                # Save if missing; otherwise skip unless --refeed.
140	                if abs_path.exists() and not refeed:
141	                    total_skip += 1
142	                    continue
143	                try:
144	                    if not abs_path.exists():
145	                        w, h = _save_image(img, abs_path)
146	                    else:
147	                        with Image.open(abs_path) as existing:
148	                            w, h = existing.size
149	                except Exception as e:
150	                    log.warning("save failed id=%s: %s", doc_id, e)
151	                    continue
152	                jpeg_bytes = abs_path.read_bytes()
153	                pil_images.append(Image.open(abs_path).convert("RGB"))
154	                pending.append({
155	                    "id": doc_id,
156	                    "filename": f"{doc_id}.jpg",
157	                    "path": rel,
158	                    "split": split,
159	                    "label": int(ex.get("label", -1) or -1),
160	                    "width": w,
161	                    "height": h,
162	                    "full_image": base64.b64encode(jpeg_bytes).decode("ascii"),
163	                })
164	
165	            if not pending:
166	                continue
167

1	"""Run a reverse-image-search query against a deployed Vespa application.
2	
3	Loads the same DINOv2 model used by the feeder, embeds the input image, packs
4	the binary version, and runs a `nearestNeighbor(embedding_binary, q_bin)`
5	query with the `closeness` rank profile — same path the demo's backend uses.
6	
7	Environment
8	-----------
9	    RIS_VESPA_URL        Vespa endpoint (e.g. http://localhost:8080 for local
10	                         Docker, or the mTLS URL printed by `vespa deploy` for
11	                         Vespa Cloud). Required.
12	    RIS_VESPA_CERT_PATH  Optional. Path to data-plane public cert (Vespa Cloud).
13	    RIS_VESPA_KEY_PATH   Optional. Path to data-plane private key (Vespa Cloud).
14	    RIS_MODEL_NAME       Default: facebook/dinov2-base.
15	    RIS_DEVICE           Default: auto (cuda → mps → cpu).
16	
17	Usage
18	-----
19	    python search.py path/to/query.jpg --hits 10 --ranking hybrid
20	"""
21	from __future__ import annotations
22	
23	import argparse
24	import io
25	import json
26	import os
27	from pathlib import Path
28	
29	import numpy as np
30	import torch
31	from PIL import Image
32	from transformers import AutoImageProcessor, AutoModel
33	from vespa.application import Vespa
34	
35	
36	_RANKING_PROFILES = {
37	    "hybrid":         "closeness",                # binary HNSW first-phase + float rerank top 100
38	    "hybrid_strict":  "closeness_hybrid_strict",  # same, rerank top 1000
39	    "binary":         "closeness_binary",         # binary HNSW only, no rerank
40	    "weighted":       "closeness_weighted",       # binary HNSW first-phase + α·float + (1−α)·binary rerank
41	}
42	
43	
44	def _device(requested: str) -> str:
45	    if requested != "auto":
46	        return requested
47	    if torch.cuda.is_available():
48	        return "cuda"
49	    if torch.backends.mps.is_available():
50	        return "mps"
51	    return "cpu"
52	
53	
54	def _embed(image_path: Path, model_name: str, device: str) -> np.ndarray:
55	    processor = AutoImageProcessor.from_pretrained(model_name)
56	    model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name).to(device).eval()
57	    img = Image.open(image_path).convert("RGB")
58	    with torch.inference_mode():
59	        batch = processor(images=[img], return_tensors="pt").to(device)
60	        out = model(**batch)
61	        cls = out.last_hidden_state[:, 0]
62	        cls = torch.nn.functional.normalize(cls, dim=-1)
63	    return cls.detach().to("cpu", dtype=torch.float32).numpy()[0]
64	
65	
66	def _pack_binary(emb: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
67	    """Sign-bit pack 768 floats into 96 int8s — matches the schema's
68	    `binarize | pack_bits` indexing pipeline so the query tensor is
69	    bit-aligned with the indexed `embedding_binary` field."""
70	    bits = (emb > 0).astype(np.uint8)
71	    return np.packbits(bits).view(np.int8)
72	
73	
74	def _search(
75	    app: Vespa,
76	    embedding: np.ndarray,
77	    hits: int,
78	    target_hits: int,
79	    ranking: str,
80	    alpha: float | None,
81	) -> dict:
82	    profile = _RANKING_PROFILES[ranking]
83	    binary_q = _pack_binary(embedding)
84	    body = {
85	        "yql": (
86	            f"select * from image where "
87	            f"{{targetHits:{target_hits}}}nearestNeighbor(embedding_binary, q_bin)"
88	        ),
89	        "input.query(q)":     embedding.astype(np.float32).tolist(),
90	        "input.query(q_bin)": binary_q.astype(int).tolist(),
91	        "ranking.profile":    profile,
92	        "hits":               hits,
93	        "presentation.summary": "id-only",
94	    }
95	    if ranking == "weighted" and alpha is not None:
96	        body["input.query(alpha)"] = float(alpha)
97	    response = app.query(body=body)
98	    if not response.is_successful():
99	        raise RuntimeError(f"Vespa query failed: {response.get_json()}")
100	    return response.json
101	
102	
103	def main() -> None:
104	    p = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
105	    p.add_argument("image", type=Path, help="Path to the query image")
106	    p.add_argument("--hits", type=int, default=10)
107	    p.add_argument("--target-hits", type=int, default=200,
108	                   help="targetHits for nearestNeighbor — affects HNSW exploration depth")
109	    p.add_argument("--ranking", choices=list(_RANKING_PROFILES), default="hybrid")
110	    p.add_argument("--alpha", type=float, default=0.7,
111	                   help="weight on float closeness in the `weighted` profile (1-α on binary)")
112	    args = p.parse_args()
113	
114	    url = os.environ["RIS_VESPA_URL"].rstrip("/")
115	    cert = os.environ.get("RIS_VESPA_CERT_PATH") or None
116	    key = os.environ.get("RIS_VESPA_KEY_PATH") or None
117	    kwargs: dict = {"url": url}
118	    if cert and key:
119	        kwargs["cert"] = cert
120	        kwargs["key"] = key
121	    app = Vespa(**kwargs)
122	
123	    model_name = os.environ.get("RIS_MODEL_NAME", "facebook/dinov2-base")
124	    device = _device(os.environ.get("RIS_DEVICE", "auto"))
125	    embedding = _embed(args.image, model_name, device)
126	
127	    payload = _search(app, embedding, args.hits, args.target_hits, args.ranking, args.alpha)
128	    children = (payload.get("root") or {}).get("children") or []
129	    for hit in children:
130	        fields = hit.get("fields") or {}
131	        mf = fields.get("matchfeatures") or {}
132	        print(json.dumps({
133	            "id":               fields.get("id"),
134	            "filename":         fields.get("filename"),
135	            "split":            fields.get("split"),
136	            "label":            fields.get("label"),
137	            "score":            hit.get("relevance"),
138	            "binary_closeness": mf.get("closeness(field,embedding_binary)"),
139	            "float_closeness":  mf.get("closeness_emb"),
140	        }))
141	
142	
143	if __name__ == "__main__":
144	    main()

5	import sys
